intended_object: The 26-dimensional standard (defining) representation of the scalar extension to k of the short-root F₄ carrier. The carrier is a closed subgroup scheme of GL₂₆ over 𝔽₂. The representation is a right comodule over its coordinate Hopf algebra on k²⁶. This reading comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The standard representation of a closed subgroup G ⊆ GL_n is the defining representation of GL_n restricted to G. In comodule terms, the coaction v ↦ Σ e_i ⊗ X_{ij} on k^n of the GL_n coordinate Hopf algebra is pushed forward along the restriction map k[GL_n] → k[G].

The definition does exactly this. `coordinateMap k` is the base change to k of the quotient map k[GL₂₆]/𝔽₂ → k[GL₂₆]/I, where I is the carrier's defining Hopf ideal. It is transported along the identification of the base change of k[GL₂₆] over 𝔽₂ with k[GL₂₆] over k. `GeneralLinear.corestrictStandardComodule` then applies `Comodule.Corestrict` along this Hopf algebra map to the standard GL₂₆ comodule, which is built from the generic matrix. Because the map is surjective, the representation is faithful, as the file proves next.

The object is a specific representation of a specific group scheme. The hypothesis `[Algebra (ZMod 2) k]` is needed because the carrier is defined over 𝔽₂, and k is otherwise an arbitrary commutative ring, so the generality is not too narrow. Mathlib has no comodule-theoretic standard representation of such group schemes.
